startup: Operator starts SOMA through the supported launcher or equivalent local control.
The Python host creates a fresh run identity and acquires exclusive ownership of the canonical data instance.
Configuration and local trust prerequisites are loaded and validated.
HLD-02 persistence readiness runs: authoritative connection policy, migration/integrity validation, and required recovery gating complete before authoritative service is exposed.
Application services, domain modules, adapters, and the background-job coordinator initialize against the ready data instance.
The host selects/binds a supported exact loopback origin only.
HLD-13 runtime-registry/readiness evidence is published atomically and verified by the launcher through the authenticated exact-origin health protocol.
Only after successful verification does the launcher open or focus the browser UI.
interactive_command: Browser sends a same-origin command request to the local application boundary.
Application boundary authenticates/validates transport context and deserializes a versioned request contract.
Application service loads required authoritative state and invokes the owning domain policy.
HLD-14 transaction/audit rules and HLD-02 persistence interfaces commit the accepted mutation atomically.
Response returns canonical result/revision/projection data to the browser.
Browser renders the result but does not become authority for the accepted mutation.
interactive_query: Browser sends a same-origin query request.
Application/query service reads authoritative state through owned persistence/query interfaces.
Derived projections are computed reproducibly from owning-domain truth.
Response returns presentation data without creating a second mutable source of truth.
adapter_ingestion: Manual or scheduled discovery invokes a source-family adapter inside the host runtime boundary.
Adapter reads untrusted local source material without authoritative domain mutation.
Parsed/normalized observations are staged with provenance and validation findings.
Review/auto-accept policy selects only governed accepted proposals.
Accepted changes re-enter through the same application-service/domain transaction path as manual commands.
background_job: The host's background coordinator discovers runnable durable jobs according to the owning domain/runtime policy.
Before material work, restart-safe phase/checkpoint state is persisted through HLD-02.
Long work may call adapters or application services but never bypass domain mutation policy.
Each authoritative checkpoint/mutation commits through normal transaction and audit boundaries.
Browser presence is not required for job continuity; progress is a projection of durable/runtime job state.
browser_restart: Browser tab/window may close, reload, crash, or reopen independently.
The authoritative host, jobs, and persistence remain running until an explicit host stop or fatal runtime failure.
A reopened browser verifies/uses the current exact local origin and reloads current projections rather than relying on stale client memory.
shutdown: Operator requests Stop/Exit through an authenticated supported local control such as tray or direct stop launcher.
HLD-13 revalidates that the target is the exact current SOMA run before control is accepted.
The host stops accepting new material commands and signals cancellable/background work to checkpoint or finish according to job policy.
In-flight authoritative transactions complete or roll back; no partial mutation is created by shutdown.
HLD-02 closes authoritative persistence connections and releases canonical data-instance ownership.
Runtime readiness/registry state is retired so stale PID/port/registry evidence cannot represent a live instance.
Forced termination is only a separately governed fallback after fresh identity revalidation and graceful shutdown failure.

transport_shape.browser_to_host: same-origin loopback HTTP using versioned JSON contracts; exact server/framework selection is LLD-01
transport_shape.host_to_local_sources: narrow adapter interfaces to local files/OS facilities
